mainTopic: The condition 'שירצה אבא', and how far we trust a claimant, a father, or a woman about קידושין, including for סקילה
overview: The amud begins by finishing the גמרא's discussion of the condition 'on condition that my father wants.' The גמרא first reads it as 'my father stays silent,' then as 'my father will not object.' רבי ינאי accepts that this splits the משנה into two cases, and ריש לקיש draws a rule from that. רב יוסף בר אמי instead keeps one case, with a thirty-day window for the father to object. A new משנה then teaches that when a father forgot whom his daughter was betrothed to, a man who claims 'I betrothed her' is believed. If two men make the claim, both give a גט, or one gives a גט and the other marries her. רב says a lone claimant may give a גט but not marry her, while רב אסי, backed by a ברייתא, says he may even marry her. When the woman herself says she does not know, the claimant may not marry her, because she may be covering for him. The גמרא then asks whether the father's word can lead to סקילה. רב, רב אסי and רב חסדא disagree, and the amud ends as a ברייתא supporting רב חסדא begins.

steps.title: First suggestion: the condition means father stays silent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that 'on condition that my father wants' really means 'on condition that my father stays silent.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: on condition that my father stays silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its first answer to the question 'what does על מנת שירצה אבא mean?' Its answer is that the condition is only that the father keeps quiet and does not protest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle clause of the משנה says that if the father died, she is betrothed, even though he never said 'yes.' That makes sense if 'want' only means 'stay silent': he never protested, so the condition is met.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that, a condition attached to the קידושין
That he will stay silent
My father

phrases.english: On condition that my father stays silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the גמרא's proposed definition of the condition, which began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly must the father do for the condition 'שירצה אבא' to be fulfilled?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He only needs to stay silent and not protest.

steps.title: The last clause shows silence is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The last clause of the משנה says that if the son dies, we teach the father to say he does not want the קידושין. Why should that help if he already stayed silent?
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last clause: if the son died, we teach the father to say that he does not want it. Why does that work? He already stayed silent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'silence' reading by pointing to the last clause of the משנה. If silence were enough, the condition would already be fulfilled, and the father could not undo it later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'silence' reading, once the father heard and kept quiet, the condition was met and the קידושין became final. Yet the משנה lets him protest later, after the son dies, and undo the קידושין (so she is not left tied to the son's brother through יבום). That shows his earlier silence did not lock anything in.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last clause, a signal that the גמרא is checking the end of the משנה
We teach / instruct (someone what to say)
Why?
But he was silent!

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
If the son died, we instruct the father
phrases.notes: The 'son' is the man who made the קידושין depend on his father's wishes.

phrases.english: to say that he does not want it.
Why? But he was silent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'silence' definition from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the condition only requires the father's silence.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If silence fulfilled the condition, the father's later protest after the son's death should not matter. The משנה says it does matter.

steps.title: New reading: father must never object
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading: the son said 'on condition that my father will not object,' which stays open at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said to her: 'On condition that my father will not object.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'silence' reading and replaces it. Now the condition is 'as long as my father does not object,' and the father keeps the right to object later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the father can object at any time, the last clause works: after the son dies, the father can still object and undo the קידושין. The middle clause works too: if the father dies, he can never object, so she stays betrothed. But this new reading does not fit the first clause well, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a signal that an earlier idea is being replaced
That he will not protest / object

phrases.english: Rather, he said to her:
'On condition that my father will not object.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by redefining the condition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The condition only required the father to stay silent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition is that the father will not object, and he can object at any time.

steps.title: Does the משנה now speak of two different cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the first clause must follow one meaning while the middle and last clauses follow another.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the first clause follows one reason, and the middle and last clauses follow another reason!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem with the new reading. The first clause still needs the 'silence' meaning, while the rest needs the 'no objection' meaning, so one משנה is split into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause ('if the father wanted, she is betrothed; if not, she is not') fits the 'silence' condition: if the father stayed silent when he heard, she is betrothed; if he objected right away, she is not. The middle and last clauses fit a man whose condition was 'my father will not object.' The גמרא is surprised that one smooth משנה would quietly switch cases partway through.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
The middle clause
Reason; here, a different setup or case

phrases.english: The first clause follows one reason,
and the middle and last clauses follow another reason!
phrases.notes: Literally 'one reason' both times, but the גמרא means two different ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא בְּחַד טַעְמָא וּמְצִיעֲתָא וְסֵיפָא בְּחַד טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3 for splitting the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It forces one משנה to describe two different conditions, which seems unlikely.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: Yes, it is two cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי accepts the split: the משנה really does speak of two different cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי answers the objection by simply agreeing with it. Yes, the first clause is one case and the rest is another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of looking for a way to fit everything into one case, רבי ינאי accepts the split. In his view, two cases inside one משנה is not a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by accepting its point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenger's description as correct
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Splitting the משנה into two cases is a weakness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה really does contain two cases, and that is acceptable.

steps.title: ריש לקיש draws a rule for explaining a משנה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns from רבי ינאי that we prefer two cases with one תנא over one case with two תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Learn from this that, according to רבי ינאי, we push ourselves to explain a משנה as two cases by one תנא, rather than as two תנאים with one case.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש takes רבי ינאי's 'yes' and turns it into a general rule. When a משנה is hard to explain, we would rather say it speaks of two different cases than say two different תנאים wrote it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two ways to handle the משנה: keep one case but say the clauses come from two תנאים who disagree, or keep one תנא and say the clauses describe two cases. רבי ינאי chose the second, even though it is a stretch. ריש לקיש notes this shows which option רבי ינאי prefers.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this
We push / strain (to explain something)
We set up / explain (a source as speaking about)
According to
A תנא, a sage of the משנה / תנאים, several such sages

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ינאי, keeping a משנה with one author matters more than keeping it about one case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general tool for explaining any משנה: when forced to choose, רבי ינאי splits the cases rather than the authors.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: Learn from this
that according to Rabbi Yannai we push ourselves
and explain the Mishnah as two reasons
phrases.notes: 'Two reasons' here means two different cases.

phrases.english: and following one tanna,
and we do not explain it as two tanna'im
and one reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from רבי ינאי's answer in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי ינאי, we prefer to explain a משנה as two cases by one תנא rather than one case split between two תנאים.

steps.title: רב יוסף בר אמי: one case, no objection for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר אמי keeps the whole משנה as one case: the condition is that the father does not object within thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר אמי said: Really it is all one case. What does 'on condition that my father wants' mean? On condition that my father does not object from now until thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף בר אמי offers a different answer to the objection of step 4. He explains the condition so that every clause of the משנה fits a single case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause, 'wanted' means he stayed quiet for thirty days, and 'if not' means he objected within them. If the father dies within the thirty days without objecting, she stays betrothed (middle clause). If the son dies within the thirty days, the father can still object (last clause). So there is no need to split the משנה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually, a signal of keeping an earlier idea
What (does it mean)?
Thirty days

steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to read 'שירצה אבא': רבי ינאי splits the משנה into two cases; רב יוסף בר אמי keeps one case with a thirty-day window to object.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Ami said:
Really, it is one reason,
and what does 'on condition that my father wants' mean?
On condition that my father does not object
from now until thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם חַד טַעְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 4 than רבי ינאי did in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the condition so all clauses fit one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must be split into two cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition is no objection within thirty days, which fits the entire משנה as one case.

steps.title: New משנה: father forgot to whom he betrothed his daughter
steps.stepSummary: A father says he betrothed his daughter but does not know to whom; if one man comes and says 'I betrothed her,' he is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A father says, 'I betrothed my daughter, but I do not know to whom I betrothed her.' One man comes and says, 'I betrothed her.' He is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that when a father forgot whom his daughter is betrothed to, a single man who claims to be that man is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father knows she is betrothed but cannot name the man. When one man steps forward with the claim, the משנה accepts it, and no one contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the start of a new משנה
I betrothed (gave in קידושין)
Believed / trusted

phrases.english: MISHNAH: 'I betrothed my daughter,
but I do not know to whom I betrothed her,'
and one man came and said,
'I betrothed her,' he is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ קִדַּשְׁתִּי אֶת בִּתִּי וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ לְמִי קִידַּשְׁתִּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה, unrelated to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the father does not know to whom he betrothed his daughter, one man who claims to have betrothed her is believed.

steps.title: Two men each claim they betrothed her
steps.stepSummary: If two men each say 'I betrothed her,' both must give a גט. If they wish, one gives a גט and the other marries her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this one says 'I betrothed her' and that one says 'I betrothed her,' both give a גט. And if they want, one gives a גט and the other marries her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a harder case: two men both claim to be the husband. Since we cannot tell which one is right, both must give a גט, unless one gives a גט and the other marries her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here neither claim can simply be believed, because they contradict each other. If both give a גט, she is free to marry anyone. If only one gives a גט, she may marry the other one, since whichever man was the real husband, the situation is now taken care of.

keyTerms.meaning: A bill of divorce
Marries her (takes her in as his wife)
Both of them

steps.whatToRemember: One claimant is believed. Two claimants: both give a גט, or one gives a גט and the other marries her.

phrases.english: If this one said, 'I betrothed her,'
and that one said, 'I betrothed her,'
both of them give a bill of divorce.
And if they want, one gives a bill of divorce,
and the other one marries her.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אָמַר אֲנִי קִידַּשְׁתִּיהָ וְזֶה אָמַר אֲנִי קִידַּשְׁתִּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה from one claimant to two competing claimants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two men claim to have betrothed her, both give a גט, or one gives a גט and the other may marry her.

steps.title: רב: Believed to divorce her, not to marry her
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the man who claims 'I betrothed her' is believed only enough to give a גט, not to marry her. The גמרא explains both halves of his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: he is believed to give a גט, but he is not believed to marry her. Why is he believed to give a גט? Because a person does not sin when he gains nothing from it. Why is he not believed to marry her? Because we worry that his desire for her pushed him to lie.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with רב's reading of the משנה about the man who says 'I betrothed her.' It also gives the reasoning behind each half of his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving a גט brings the man no benefit, so he has no reason to lie, and we trust him that far. Marrying her is something he might want, so his claim could be driven by desire. That is why we do not trust him enough to let him marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: Believed; his word is accepted
To marry (to take her as his wife)
A person does not sin without gaining something for himself
His desire overpowers him

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav says:
He is believed to give a get,
but he is not believed to marry her.
He is believed to give a get,
because a person does not sin when it is not for himself.
And why is he not believed to marry her?
Say that his desire overpowers him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נֶאֱמָן לִיתֵּן גֵּט וְאֵין נֶאֱמָן לִכְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far the man in Step 8 is believed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The claimant is believed to give a גט but not to marry her, since desire may have led him to lie.

steps.title: רב אסי: Believed even to marry her
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי disagrees with רב and says the man is believed even to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי says: he is believed even to marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives the opposing view. The man's claim is fully accepted, so he may marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב worried that desire would make the man lie. רב אסי does not share that worry in this case, so the man's word counts for everything, including marrying her.

keyTerms.meaning: Even; also

phrases.english: Rav Asi says:
He is believed even to marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַסִּי אָמַר אַף נֶאֱמָן לִכְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's limit in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The claimant is believed even to marry her.

steps.title: רב אסי agrees when the woman herself does not know
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי admits that if the woman herself says she does not know whom she was betrothed to, the man who claims her may not marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי agrees about a woman who says, 'I was betrothed, but I do not know to whom.' If one man comes and says, 'I betrothed her,' he is not believed to marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב אסי's view has a limit. When the woman, not the father, is the one who does not know, even רב אסי says the man may not marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only thing that changed is who is speaking: the woman herself instead of her father. This change is enough to take away the man's right to marry her. Step 16 gives the reason: she may be covering for him.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (admits in this case)
I was betrothed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the earlier case the FATHER does not know whom he betrothed his daughter to. Here the WOMAN HERSELF says she does not know.

phrases.english: And Rav Asi agrees
in the case of a woman who says: 'I was betrothed
and I do not know to whom I was betrothed,'
and one man came and said 'I betrothed her,'
that he is not believed to marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on רב אסי's ruling from Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the woman herself does not know, the claimant may not marry her, even according to רב אסי.

steps.title: The משנה lets one of them marry her: a refutation of רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from the משנה, which says that one man gives a גט and the other may marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if they wish, one gives a גט and the other marries her. This is a refutation of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's view using the case of two claimants (Step 9). There the משנה lets one of the claimants marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a man who claims 'I betrothed her' may not marry her. Yet the משנה allows one of the two claimants to marry her, which seems to contradict רב directly.

keyTerms.meaning: If they wish
A strong refutation

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah:
If they wish, one gives a get
and the other marries her.
This is a refutation of Rav!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן רָצוּ אֶחָד נוֹתֵן גֵּט וְאֶחָד כּוֹנֵס תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה from Step 9 to challenge רב's ruling in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the claimant may not marry her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows a claimant to marry her, which goes against רב.

steps.title: רב: With a rival claimant, he is afraid to lie
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the משנה's case is different. Because another man is also claiming her, each man is afraid to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can say to you: there it is different. Since there is another man with him, he is really afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by showing that the two-claimant case is a special situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a man claims her alone, nobody is there to challenge him, so desire might lead him to lie. When a second man is also claiming her, each one fears being caught, so we can trust him enough to let him marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: There it is different
He is truly afraid

phrases.english: Rav can say to you:
There it is different,
since there is another man with him,
he is truly afraid.
phrases.notes: He is afraid to lie, because the other claimant could expose him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: a rival claimant creates fear of lying.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's permission to marry seemed to contradict רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: When there is a second claimant, the man is afraid to lie, so he may marry her. When he claims her alone, רב's rule still holds.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that the claimant may even marry her. If a second man later claims her, he cannot make her forbidden to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught according to רב אסי: a father says, 'I betrothed my daughter, but I do not know to whom.' One man came and said, 'I betrothed her.' He is believed even to marry her. If he married her and then another man came and said, 'I betrothed her,' the second man does not have the power to make her forbidden to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב אסי's view word for word: 'he is believed even to marry her.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case is exactly the father-does-not-know case, and it allows marriage, as רב אסי said. It adds that once the first man has married her, a later claim cannot undo the marriage or forbid her to him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught (in a ברייתא) according to his view
He married her
It is not in his power
To make her forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רב says the lone claimant may give a גט but not marry her, because his desire might make him lie. רב אסי says he may even marry her, and a ברייתא supports him. רב explains the משנה's two-claimant case by saying fear of the rival keeps each man honest.

phrases.english: It is taught in a Baraita according to Rav Asi:
'I betrothed my daughter
and I do not know to whom I betrothed her,'
and one man came and said 'I betrothed her':
he is believed even to marry her.
If he married her, and another man came
and said 'I betrothed her,'
it is not in his power to forbid her to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the husband, the first man who already married her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב אסי's view from Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's ruling that the claimant may even marry her
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states 'אַף נֶאֱמָן לִכְנוֹס' in the father's case

steps.title: The woman's own claim: the man who claims her may not marry her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If a woman says she was betrothed but does not know to whom, a man who says he betrothed her is not believed to marry her, because she may be covering for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who said, "I was betrothed, but I don't know to whom," and then a man came and said, "I betrothed her": he is not believed to marry her, because she is covering for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 15 goes on to a second case, where it is the woman, not the father, who says she was betrothed to someone unknown. Here the man who claims her is not believed to marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches exactly what רב אסי admitted in step 12, so the ברייתא supports him on this point too. The reason is new: she may now like this man and quietly go along with his claim, even if someone else really betrothed her. A father has no such personal pull, so in his case the claimant can be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Believed; trusted on his word
To marry her (to bring her into his home as his wife)
She covers for him; she backs up his claim for her own reasons

phrases.english: A woman who said: "I became betrothed
but I do not know to whom I became betrothed"
and one man came and said: "I betrothed her"
he is not believed to marry her.
Because she is covering for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁאָמְרָה ״נִתְקַדַּשְׁתִּי וְאֵינִי יוֹדַעַת לְמִי נִתְקַדַּשְׁתִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 15, now with the case of the woman's own claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's admission (step 12) that when the woman herself says she does not know whom she was betrothed to, the claimant may not marry her.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the ברייתא, which rules that the claimant is not believed to marry her because she may be covering for him.

steps.title: Would the father's word lead to stoning?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: when the father says he betrothed his daughter, is his word strong enough that she would be stoned if she later sleeps with another man?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What is the law about stoning her based on the father's word?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the father in the משנה. Is his claim strong enough for a court to give the death penalty of סקילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the question was only whether the father's word makes her forbidden to other men. Now the גמרא asks if his word can go all the way to a death penalty. Forbidding someone is much less serious than executing her.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them; the scholars raised a question they were unsure about
To stone (the death penalty of סקילה, given to a betrothed girl who commits adultery)
Based on him; relying on his testimony

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
What is the law about stoning based on him?
phrases.notes: "Him" is the father from the משנה, who says he betrothed his daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִסְקוֹל עַל יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether people may marry her to a new question about the death penalty.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the father's claim that he betrothed his daughter enough for the court to stone her for adultery?

steps.title: רב says no stoning; רב אסי says stoning
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the court does not stone her based on the father's word. רב אסי rules that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: We do not stone her. רב אסי said: We do stone her.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, and they disagree. רב says no stoning, and רב אסי says stoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pair who disagreed earlier about marrying her (steps 10 to 14). Here they give only their rulings, and the next step explains the reason behind each one.

keyTerms.meaning: We stone; the court carries out סקילה
We do not stone

phrases.english: Rav said: We do not stone.
And Rav Asi said: We stone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: אֵין סוֹקְלִין. וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: סוֹקְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: the court does not stone her based on the father's word. רב אסי: the court does stone her.

steps.title: The reasons behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that the Torah believes the father only to make her forbidden, not to put her to death. רב אסי holds that the Torah believes the father for everything, including the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said we do not stone: when the Torah believed the father, it was only to make her forbidden, not to kill her. רב אסי said we stone: the Torah believed the father for the whole matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each one ruled the way he did. The disagreement is about how far the Torah's trust in a father goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the Torah trusts the father when he says "I gave my daughter to this man". רב limits that trust to the prohibition, so his word cannot be used to take a life. רב אסי says that once the Torah trusts the father, it trusts him fully, so the court may stone her.

keyTerms.meaning: Believed him; trusted him
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
For a prohibition; to make her forbidden
For killing; for the death penalty
For the whole matter; in every way

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: a person can be trusted enough to forbid something but not enough to lead to a death penalty, which needs a higher standard.

phrases.english: Rav said: We do not stone,
because when the Merciful One believed the father,
it was for the prohibition; for killing, He did not believe him.
Rav Asi said: We stone,
for the whole matter the Merciful One believed the father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two rulings in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the father is trusted only for the prohibition, not for the death penalty. רב אסי: the father is trusted for everything, including stoning.

steps.title: רב אסי agrees: no stoning based on the woman's own word
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי admits that if the woman herself says "I became betrothed", the court does not stone her based on that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: I agree that if the woman herself says "I was betrothed", we do not stone her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי sets a limit on his own ruling. The father's word can lead to stoning, but the woman's own statement cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's special trust belongs to the father, not to the woman. So even רב אסי agrees that her own claim does not lead to the death penalty. This sets up the problem he raises in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: I agree; I admit
A woman who says
I became betrothed

phrases.english: Rav Asi said: And I agree
in the case of a woman who says "I became betrothed",
that we do not stone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אסי limits his ruling from step 19 so that it does not cover the woman's own claim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the woman herself says she was betrothed, she is not stoned based on her own word.

steps.title: רב אסי admits his own rulings seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says his rulings are "roof-breakers". He shows with a קל וחומר that they seem to contradict each other: the woman's case is stricter for marriage, yet he rules more leniently about stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: These rulings of mine break roofs. In a case where a man who comes to marry her may marry her, you say we stone. Then in a case where a man who comes to marry her may not marry her, isn't it logical that we stone?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי challenges himself. He points out that his own rulings do not seem to fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the father's case (step 11), a claimant may marry her, so the father's word is the weaker restriction, yet רב אסי says she is stoned. In the woman's case (step 12), no claimant may marry her, which is stricter, so by קל וחומר she should surely be stoned. But in step 20 he said she is not stoned, and that is the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Teachings; rulings
They break roofs; they are very hard to understand
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
Isn't it logical? (the opening of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אסי is not attacking רב here. He is challenging his own two rulings, which seem to point in opposite directions.

phrases.english: And Rav Asi said:
These teachings of mine
break roofs.
phrases.notes: A picture for rulings so hard to understand that they seem to bring the roof down.

phrases.english: Now, if in a case
where if he comes to marry her, he marries her,
phrases.notes: This is the father's case, where he says "I betrothed her and don't know to whom" (step 11).

phrases.english: you said we stone,

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם שֶׁאִם בָּא לִכְנוֹס אֵין כּוֹנֵס
phrases.english: then in a case where if he comes to marry her, he does not marry her,
phrases.notes: This is the woman's own claim from step 12.

phrases.english: is it not logical that we stone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב אסי's admission in step 20 into a challenge against his own position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's combined rulings: stoning based on the father's word, but no stoning based on the woman's own word.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if the father's case, which is weaker for marriage because a claimant may marry her, leads to stoning, then the woman's case, which is stricter because no claimant may marry her, should surely lead to stoning too.

steps.title: The Torah trusted only the father, not the woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction: the Torah's special trust was given only to the father, so only his word can lead to סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not really a problem. The Torah trusted the father, but it did not give that same trust to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'roof-breaker' problem from the last step. It shows that רב אסי's two rulings do not actually contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed the woman's word is stronger than the father's. But the father's trust comes straight from the Torah (רחמנא), so it counts even for the death penalty. The woman can forbid herself to all men, but the Torah never gave her that special trust. So her word cannot lead to סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: the earlier claim is rejected
He believed him, He trusted him
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
To her herself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the woman is less believed about being forbidden. She does forbid herself to all men. The difference is only about punishment: the Torah gave special trust to the father, not to her.

phrases.english: But it is not so,
The Merciful One believed the father,
but her, He did not believe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by showing the קל וחומר does not work.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the source of trust: the Torah trusts the father, while the woman's word only works because she can forbid herself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the woman's word works even better for making her a married woman, it should also lead to סקילה if the father's word does.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father's trust is a special Torah rule that covers everything, even death. The woman has no such Torah trust, so her word cannot bring the death penalty.

steps.title: רב חסדא: no stoning in either case
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the court does not stone her, whether the father said he betrothed her or she said she became betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: In both cases, whether the father says it or she says it, the court does not stone her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב חסדא, gives his own ruling on the question. He says there is no סקילה in either case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי said the father's word leads to סקילה. רב חסדא disagrees and treats the father the same as the woman. Neither one's word alone is enough to give the death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
The court does not stone

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
Both this one and that one –
phrases.notes: This one is the father saying 'I betrothed my daughter.' That one is the woman saying 'I became betrothed.'

phrases.english: the court does not stone her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion next to רב and רב אסי on the question from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither the father's word nor the woman's word alone is enough for the court to stone her.

steps.title: רב חסדא is consistent: a father's word on his children's ages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows רב חסדא follows the same idea elsewhere. A father is believed about his child's age for a קרבן, but not for lashes or other punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא follows his usual reasoning. He said: If a father says 'This son of mine is nine years and one day old,' or 'This daughter of mine is three years and one day old,' he is believed for a קרבן, but not for lashes and not for other punishments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב חסדא's ruling fits another ruling of his. In both, a father's word is enough for lighter results, but not for punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine years and a day for a boy, and three years and a day for a girl, are the ages when their relations legally count. If a forbidden act happened by mistake, the father is believed about the age so the adult must bring a קרבן. But his word is not enough for מלקות or עונשין. This is the same idea as the קידושין case: a father's word cannot bring punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes according to his own reasoning, he is being consistent
Believed, trusted
An offering, brought for a sin done by mistake
Lashes
Punishments

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows רב חסדא has one clear rule: a father's word can create obligations like a קרבן, but it cannot be the basis for physical punishment.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda follows his own reasoning,
for Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּנִי זֶה בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד״,
phrases.english: "This son of mine is nine years and one day old,"

phrases.aramaic: ״בִּתִּי זוֹ בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד״ –
phrases.english: "This daughter of mine is three years and one day old" –
he is believed for an offering,
phrases.notes: The adult who sinned with the child by mistake must bring a קרבן.

phrases.english: but not for lashes and not for punishments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב חסדא's ruling in step 23 matches his other ruling about a father's word on his children's ages.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's view that a father's word does not bring punishment
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's own ruling about a father's word on his child's age: believed for a קרבן, not for מלקות or עונשין

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב חסדא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that agrees with רב חסדא, about a father saying his children are 13 and 12 years and a day old.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב חסדא: If a father says 'This son of mine is thirteen years and one day old,' or 'This daughter of mine is twelve years and one day old' –
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a support for רב חסדא from a ברייתא. Here we only see the case. The ruling of the ברייתא comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ages are the ages of adulthood: 13 and a day for a boy, 12 and a day for a girl. At these ages the child himself is responsible for what he does. The ברייתא's ruling, which continues next, will back up רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: In agreement with him
Thirteen years and one day: the age a boy becomes an adult
Twelve years and one day: the age a girl becomes an adult

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Ḥisda:

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּנִי זֶה בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד״
phrases.english: "This son of mine is thirteen years and one day old"

phrases.aramaic: ״בִּתִּי זוֹ בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד״ –
phrases.english: or "This daughter of mine is twelve years and one day old" –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an older source, a ברייתא, to back up רב חסדא's approach from steps 23-24.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that a father's word about his child does not bring punishment
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a father who says his son is 13 years and a day old or his daughter is 12 years and a day old (its ruling continues next)
